newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian president recalls former PM to form govt.
newsitem.headline: Latvian president recalls former PM to form govt.

text.p: Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis on Wednesday asked former prime minister Andris Shkele, who quit last week, to form a new government for the Baltic state.
"I have been invited by the president to form a new government," Shkele told reporters after meeting Ulmanis for more than an hour.

Shkele resigned last week, furious that Ulmanis had called on parliament to reject the premier's choice of finance minister, Vassily Melnik, who was backed by a leading party in the coalition government.
Melnik had been investigated under anti-corruption laws but the prosecutor's office subsequently said it found no wrongdoing.
Shkele's first government was formed at the end of 1995. He pledged to speed the reforms launched by Latvia after it quit the Soviet Union in 1991.
The prime minister said forming a new government would be a tough task but would not say how long he expected it to take.
Latvia's 100-seat parliament is split between 12 parties and around 10 independent deputies. No single party has anywhere near a majority.
Shkele's eight-party governing coalition had the support of around 70 members of parliament.
His rival for the prime minister's post was Economics Minister Guntar Krasts, who was proposed by the third-largest party in the former coalition.
Ulmanis asked Shkele to form a new government after several days of talks with large and small political parties.
"As a result of these consultations I consider that the majority of parties are ready to support Shkele," Ulmanis said.
Shkele has helped accelerate privatisation in Latvia as part of his aim to draw in desperately needed investment and has tried to pursue a tough monetary policy that included a balanced 1997 budget.
